evidence: describe_record uses strcpy(summary, label) into char summary[32]; main() passes argv[1] directly.
summary: Stack buffer overflow via strcpy in describe_record(): a 32-byte local buffer receives an unchecked copy of the caller-supplied label, which originates from an untrusted command-line argument in main().

validation.method: static analysis of unbounded strcpy into fixed-size stack buffer with attacker-controlled input
validation.confidence_rationale: The overflow is deterministic: any input longer than 31 characters overflows the 32-byte buffer; no runtime guard exists
validation.rubric: Unbounded copy of attacker-controlled input into a stack-allocated buffer on a program entry path
validation.evidence: describe_record calls strcpy(summary, label) where summary is char[32] and label comes from main via argv[1]
validation.counterevidence_or_proof_gap: None; the bug is structural and reproducible

attack_path.dataflow: argv[1] -> main -> describe_record(argv[1]) -> strcpy(summary, label) -> stack overflow
attack_path.reachability: The program is a CLI tool run locally; the user supplies argv[1] directly, making this trivially reachable
attack_path.impact: Stack corruption enabling potential code execution or crash; the Makefile explicitly disables hardening flags (-O0 -g, no PIE/stack protector implied)
attack_path.severity_rationale: Direct stack buffer overflow with attacker-controlled input on a trivially reachable entry path; the binary is built without hardening, increasing exploitability
attack_path.change_conditions: Replace strcpy with strncpy or snprintf with a bounded destination size, or validate input length before the copy

evidence: delete_record calls free(records[i].value) and return; lookup_record iterates by record_count and returns records[i].value without checking if it was freed.
summary: Use-after-free via dangling pointer: delete_record frees records[i].value but leaves the pointer field and record_count unchanged, so lookup_record returns freed memory for the deleted entry.

validation.method: Code review of delete_record followed by lookup_record in main
validation.confidence_rationale: The free occurs unconditionally on the matching entry; no nulling or count decrement follows; the subsequent lookup reads the dangling pointer deterministically
validation.rubric: Use of memory freed by delete_record via lookup_record returning the stale pointer
validation.evidence: delete_record calls free(records[i].value) at line 33; lookup_record at line 42 returns records[i].value which is now dangling
validation.counterevidence_or_proof_gap: None; the dangling pointer is never checked
validation.remaining_uncertainty: The freed memory may or may not still be mapped depending on allocator behavior, but the dereference is still a UAF

attack_path.dataflow: main -> delete_record("greeting") -> free(records[0].value) -> main -> lookup_record("greeting") -> return records[0].value (dangling)
attack_path.reachability: Fully reachable: main unconditionally calls delete_record then lookup_record for the same key
attack_path.impact: Reading freed heap memory; may disclose previously stored data or, in conjunction with other bugs, enable heap manipulation
attack_path.severity_rationale: The UAF is deterministic and fully reachable but the direct impact is limited to reading freed memory; exploitation requires heap state control which is harder to achieve
attack_path.change_conditions: Null the pointer and decrement record_count in delete_record, or skip already-freed entries in lookup_record

evidence: if (record_count > MAX_RECORDS) returns -1; records[record_count] is then written at index 16 when record_count equals 16, exceeding the 16-element static array.
summary: Off-by-one buffer overflow in add_record(): the guard uses record_count > MAX_RECORDS instead of >=, allowing insertion at index 16 when the table holds 16 records, writing past the end of the fixed-size array.

validation.method: Static analysis of bounds check in add_record against the array declaration
validation.confidence_rationale: The guard condition is mathematically wrong: > instead of >= allows one extra write past the array end; the array is a static local with no runtime bounds checking
validation.rubric: Off-by-one error in array bounds check permitting out-of-bounds write
validation.evidence: static struct record records[MAX_RECORDS] declares 16 elements; if (record_count > MAX_RECORDS) allows record_count==16 to proceed and writes records[16]
validation.counterevidence_or_proof_gap: None; the condition is unambiguously incorrect
validation.remaining_uncertainty: The practical impact depends on what follows the array in memory, but the write itself is an out-of-bounds access
